subject: Post-demo: Decision drivers, competitor comparisons, and smoke-validation plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Mercer <jake.mercer@medforma.com>, Chris Tan <chris.tan@medforma.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Decision drivers, competitor comparisons, and smoke-validation plan

Thanks again for carving out time today — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with your evaluation timeline.

Key pain we heard
- Token cost and latency variability on long clinical summaries (typical sequences 1k–3k tokens).
- Need for deterministic redaction and auditability for PHI-sensitive fields.
- Ability to run in your VPC (lockbox/KMS) and satisfy SOC2 evidence for the procurement team.

Goals you shared
1) Achieve parity with current vendor on extraction accuracy for SOAP notes (F1 target >= 0.87).
2) Reduce token spend by ~25% vs current baseline on summary workflows.
3) Get an on-prem / VPC pilot with audit logs and key management by Oct 15 to satisfy security review.

Competitive landscape (short summary)
- Vendor A: strong extractors but expensive at scale; limited private deployment options.
- Vendor B: cheap per token but inconsistent latency on longer context; no native KMS integration.
- Redwood: target is to balance predictable latency + cost controls (batching + intelligent caching) and provide a Private deployment path with KMS and audit logs.

Proposed smoke-validation plan (attached CSV + matrix):
- Test 1: 1k/2k/3k seq latency distribution (measure p50/p90/p99 over 500 requests). Owner: Redwood (Camila) — target p99 < 800ms on our Dedicated config.
- Test 2: Extraction accuracy head-to-head (shared 200 notes seed). Owner: MedForma (Jake) + Redwood to run eval harness.
- Test 3: Redaction audit trail validation (generate 100 redaction events, confirm log fidelity). Owner: MedForma + Security (Marissa to coordinate).
- Test 4: Cost projection using your workload mix (we'll run a simulated 30k-token/day profile). Owner: Redwood (Hannah), will supply modeling spreadsheet.

Immediate asks (can we lock these this week?):
- You to confirm the 200-note sample and an S3 location (or we can take a secure share).
- Security questionnaire: prioritize the KMS/HSM evidence — Marissa will send the list by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule the smoke run window: suggested Oct 4-6.

Attachments: MedForma-deck-brief.pdf (demo notes), MedForma-eval-criteria-matrix.xlsx, MedForma-smoke-tests.csv

Thanks — I’ll keep this short. If that all looks right, we’ll push the sample checklist + timeline into HubSpot and schedule an ops sync next week.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0184

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Decision drivers, competitor comparisons, and smoke-validation plan

On Wed, Aug 25, 2027 at 4:12 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for carving out time today — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with your evaluation timeline.
> 
> Key pain we heard
> - Token cost and latency variability on long clinical summaries (typical sequences 1k–3k tokens).

This is accurate — thanks for capturing. A couple quick clarifications and a new ask from our security lead:

Clarifications
- For Test 1, could you also include p95 and average inference memory (to understand scaling)?
- For Test 4, please include our current vendor baseline (we'll provide monthly billing/usage export).

New security ask
- Our security team requires a temporary NAT/egress whitelist plan for the pilot — can Redwood support a restrictive egress configuration for the VPC deployment? If yes, we need a short runbook describing what network endpoints are required.

Timelines
- We can provide the 200-note sample by next Tue (Aug 31).
- Oct 4-6 works for a smoke window; team will confirm next week after we check procurement calendar.

Thanks — Jake
Jake Mercer
Head of Data Platform | MedForma
Jake.Mercer@medforma.com | (650) 555-4321
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Mercer <jake.mercer@medforma.com>, Chris Tan <chris.tan@medforma.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Decision drivers, competitor comparisons, and smoke-validation plan

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the additional asks — all reasonable. Short answers and next moves: 

- We will add p95 and average inference memory to the latency report. Camila will include those columns in the smoke-tests CSV and flag the p95 target.
- Baseline billing: thanks — please drop the vendor export to the S3 share and tag the file with "baseline_vendor_usage.csv". We’ll include that in the cost model.
- Egress/NAT: yes — we support restrictive egress for the Private pilot. Marissa will draft a one-page runbook describing required endpoints and firewall rules and will attach it to the security questionnaire.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Jake: upload 200-note sample to the provided S3 location (ETA Aug 31).
- Marissa (Redwood): send security questionnaire + NAT runbook (ETA Aug 26 EOD).
- Camila (Redwood): produce updated smoke-tests.csv with p95/avg-memory columns + preliminary Dedicated config perf targets (ETA Sep 2).
- Hannah (Redwood): update HubSpot deal with timeline and push calendar invite for Oct 4 smoke window once procurement confirms.

I’ll follow up with a short Ops sync invite and attach the runbook once Marissa finishes it. If anything changes on your side, flag it here and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
